column1: # CAP-3U Currency return matrix - the declared expectation per target and case.
# `must_pass`  a PASS has been MEASURED on the toolchain that leg builds with;
# `observe`    the case is run and recorded, and fails nothing. It is the
#              verdict for a case whose behaviour is a known upstream defect.
#              Turning one into `must_pass` - or back - is a deliberate act.
# 2026-09-16), the measurement run of the 2026-09-16 mORMot pin move: that
# commit moves only the `commit =` line of mormot.lock onto
# 66d7d51c1fd21bd222b360382ed8e2b4f656aaad, so every leg built the UNPATCHED
# candidate, and every leg ran this step before it stopped at the first
# pin-derived literal elsewhere. What it measured, each on its own compiler:
# "Before" is hosted run 34241426338 at da7e1c2f, which is what this table
# declared until now: every row `must_pass` on windows-x86_64, `cur-zero-arg`
# alone on the two SysV x64 targets, nothing on macos-arm64.
# fixed currency result in mormot.core.interfaces"), written in answer to this
# project's report: on FPC SysV x64 the result is now popped out of x87 ST0,
# where FPC leaves a Currency, and on AArch64 the x0 value is no longer
# overwritten from d0. The Win64 path was already right and did not move. The
# dev host agrees on the two targets it reaches: 5/5 on Windows, and 5/5 on
# So every row is `must_pass`, and a Currency-returning service is no longer a
# documented limitation of the pin on any target.
